summary: This note is a short biographical entry on Michael Melkonian, a botanist, covering his education, academic positions and later role. It traces his studies and doctorate in Hamburg, his move to Münster as Assistant Professor, and his appointment as Full Professor and Chair of Botany at Cologne in 1988. It also lists a 1982 visiting post in the Bronx, a 1986–1988 Heisenberg Fellowship, and his directorship of the Culture Collection of Algae at Cologne since 2001.
one_line: Biography of botanist Michael Melkonian, covering his studies in Hamburg, academic posts at Münster and Cologne, and his directorship of the Culture Collection of Algae.
key_facts: Michael Melkonian studied Biology at the University of Hamburg from 1968 to 1978.
Michael Melkonian received a Diploma degree in Botany in 1974.
Michael Melkonian completed a doctorate in Botany (plant physiology) in 1978 at the University of Hamburg.
In 1978 Michael Melkonian moved to the Botany Department at the University of Münster as an Assistant Professor.
Michael Melkonian was appointed Full Professor and Chair of Botany at the University of Cologne in 1988.
In 1982 Michael Melkonian was Visiting Assistant Professor at the Albert Einstein College of Medicine of Yeshiva University in Bronx, N.Y.
From 1986 to 1988 Michael Melkonian was a Heisenberg Fellow of the German Research Foundation (DFG).
Since 2001 Michael Melkonian has been Director of the Culture Collection of Algae at the University of Cologne (CCAC).
